title: Hosted API dual-ledger per-token pilot and SQ contract matrix
creator: Ava Chen
description: Run a small-scale pricing experiment that separates ingress (input) and egress (output) token metering into two parallel ledgers, tests streaming smoothing rules and escrowed minimums, and produces a mapping matrix for our Security Questionnaire (SQ) responses tying contract minimums to billing protections.
background: Large enterprise prospects request explicit mapping between contract minimums, SQ commitments, and how streaming usage is billed. Current meter conflates IO and applies abrupt minimums that penalize chat-heavy apps. We need an experiment that validates a dual-ledger approach (separate IO ledgers), a soft-smoothing for stream bursts, and a contractual SQ matrix that legal and sales can use when negotiating reserved capacity.
objective: 1) Measure customer behavior and perceived fairness under separate input/output ledgers. 2) Validate cost symmetry assumptions and unit economics impact on host revenue. 3) Draft a Security Questionnaire mapping that ties minimum thresholds, escrow rules, and audit clauses to observed telemetry.
hypothesis: If we bill ingress and egress to separate ledgers and apply a streaming smoothing window for minimums, then high-chat customers will see fewer spiky minimum penalties and conversion to Dedicated/reserved contracts will increase by at least 8% in the pilot cohort.
success_criteria: Pilot cohort NPS (billing fairness) +10 points vs control
Reduction in billing disputes for streaming customers by 60%
At least 8% conversion-to-reserved-capacity among pilot customers within 60 days
No >2% negative impact to short-term gross margin after modeling smoothing/escrow
experiment_design: Create two billing ledgers per customer for a 90-day pilot: ledger_in (ingress tokens) and ledger_out (egress tokens). Default per-token rates are set to baseline parity for hosted SKU; run two arms: A) smoothing window of 1 hour where negative egress spikes are averaged for minimum enforcement; B) no smoothing (control). Offer optional escrowed credit: customers can pre-fund a minimal monthly escrow that absorbs up to 50% of the streaming minimum for the pilot period with prorated refunds. Instrument telemetry for token distribution, session duration, streaming handshake frequency, and billing disputes.
measurement: Primary metrics: effective ARPU, dispute count, smoothing credit utilization, conversion rate to Dedicated. Secondary metrics: average session length, percent of tokens classified as streaming vs non-streaming, latency SLO violations correlated with smoothing arm. Backfill baseline with prior 90 day cohort for matched customers.
cohort_criteria: Select 30 mid-enterprise customers (monthly spend $10k-50k) with >30% conversational streaming usage historically. Randomize into two equal arms while ensuring distribution of verticals (SaaS search, conversational agents, and call center assistants).
rollout_plan: Week 0: enable dual-ledger metering for pilot customers and communicate changes. Week 1-2: soft launch, collect telemetry, and run manual reconciliation checks. Week 3-10: full pilot. Week 11-12: analyze results and draft SQ contract matrix. Post-week 12: prepare proposal for either 6-month extension or production rollout.
rollout_triggers: No more than 5% of pilot customers report critical billing errors in first 2 weeks
Real-time billing ingestion pipeline latency < 30s for pilot customers
Legal review sign-off on escrow terms and refund flows
legal_security_notes: Escrowed minimums create a custodial relationship; legal to define escrow custody, refunds, and auditability. SQ matrix must reference data residency, audit trail retention for billing events, KMS usage for billing keys, and obligations around forensic logs. Coordinate with Security and Legal to produce 1-page SQ mapping per standard RFP template.
open_questions: What is the canonical definition of 'streaming token' across SDKs and proxies?
How to pro-rate escrow refunds for partial-month cancellations?
Should smoothing apply symmetrically to ingress and egress or only to egress?
What SLA language needs to be added to SQ about dispute resolution timelines and audit artifacts?
